block.intro.heading: You rebuild the story before you build anything
block.intro.body: The chat that held the plan is closed, so the first afternoon goes into remembering what you were building. **That afternoon is the cost, and it never appears in a budget.**
block.intro.imageAlt: A desk lamp glowing amber over an open notebook and a closed laptop at three in the morning, with a window full of stars behind the desk.
block.intro.caption: The hour when the only person who knows the plan is the one who left it.
block.problem.heading: You keep re-explaining the same project
block.problem.body: You type the purpose into session one, then session two, then into a third agent that knows nothing about the first two. **Each retelling drops something.**
block.impact.heading: The record goes missing on the way in
block.impact.body: HaluMem measured memory update accuracy below 50% in every system it tested. Nothing dramatic happens when you ask the question. The record was never written.
block.answer.heading: Agents coordinate, you keep every decision
block.answer.body: Agent Custom Setup is five small repositories that give your coding agents a shared memory, a shared ticket log, and shared version control. **One command brings an agent up to speed on the whole project.**
block.acs.heading: Two agents should not discover the collision afterwards
block.acs.body: ACS runs the tickets: makes them workable, breaks them down, and hands each piece over with one shared, versioned install surface behind it. **When two agents disagree, a person settles it.**
block.oio.heading: Your note should not look like a note an agent wrote about itself
block.oio.body: OIO owns the ticket form and nothing else. Every issue carries a required, machine-checkable filer stamp answering who initiated the filing and whose identity is on it. **An agent cannot promote its own note from the body text.**
block.pcm.heading: The next session should not have to ask you what the project is
block.pcm.body: PCM keeps tasks, checkpoints, push receipts and pull-request gates as repository state, so a fresh session recovers purpose, current state, bounded task, evidence, blockers and the next action without prior conversation history. **The handoff is a file.**
block.cgm.heading: A finished repository can still be unreadable
block.cgm.body: CGM routes the writing: which module a README uses, what voice a pull request gets, what an image is for. When the evidence is missing, the output has to say so. **A citation proves traceability, not truth.**
block.train.heading: One version set, read from one place
block.train.body: train holds the certified version set. Measured on 2026-10-01, one pin lived in thirteen files across three revisions. **No product repository certifies its own siblings.**
block.compare.heading: What you have now is a chat window
block.compare.body: One conversation holds the plan, a branch name holds the state, your memory holds who agreed to what. The stack puts a ticket with a filer stamp, a checkpoint a fresh session can read, and one version pin in the repository instead.
block.measure.heading: No benchmark of this stack exists yet
block.measure.body: Another lab measured agent memory, and published its own limits with the number. ACS claims something structural: status, ownership and the filer sit on the item, and retrieval reads them back. Whether that moves write-time omission, update accuracy, or the 55.2% ceiling is untested.
block.measure.tagNote: Held as a hypothesis. No product benchmark behind it.
block.boundaries.heading: Some decisions stay yours on purpose
block.boundaries.body: Four limits worth knowing before you spend an afternoon on this.
block.boundaries.items: Adjudication and tie-breaking between agents was JEV's job. JEV is not strong enough for it yet and is parked in jev-dump, so a disagreement between two agents still needs a person.
train carries a proposed status. OIO's pins point at it and preserve that status.
hivemind/research is a research corpus. Nobody should read its findings as a feature list.
There is no live GitHub sync. The facts are current as of 2026-10-13.
block.boundaries.proof: No adoption figure exists yet, so none is published.

research.heading: Agent memory fails before it retrieves
research.intro: The damage happens on the way in, before retrieval gets a chance to help.
research.tag.measured: A number from a cited primary source
research.noStatusHeading: Systems with no status field at all
research.pcm.heading: Update accuracy never cleared half
research.pcm.body: PCM keeps the write path as repository state. That is where agent memory fails, in every system tested.
research.pcm.chartTitle: Update accuracy stayed below 50% in every system tested
research.pcm.chartSubtitle: Memory update accuracy across five agent-memory systems, HaluMem benchmark
research.pcm.chartCaption: Omission rates in the same benchmark ran from 52% to 94%. Hallucinations accumulate during the extraction and updating stages, then propagate errors to the question answering stage.
research.pcm.chartAlt: Horizontal bars showing memory update accuracy: Zep 47.3 percent, Mem0 25.5 percent, Mem0-Graph 24.5 percent, Supermemory 16.4 percent, Memobase 5.2 percent. A reference line at 50 percent is above every bar.
research.pcm.statWriteLabel: of memory failures are write-time omissions
research.pcm.statExtractLabel: points lost to extraction versus verbatim storage
research.pcm.statExtractBody: Extraction costs 15.9 points on LoCoMo and 22.0 points on LongMemEval-S compared with storing the words as they arrived.
research.oio.heading: Almost nothing stores what it believes
research.oio.body: OIO puts the filer stamp on the item itself, machine-checkable, and requires a separate attestation before a claim can be called human.
research.oio.chartTitle: Only thirteen systems appear as exceptions, out of about seventy-three
research.oio.chartSubtitle: Systems that store a truth-status field on the item, counted by cluster
research.oio.chartCaption: Thirteen named exceptions out of about seventy-three systems. Everything else in that set has no status field, or a free-form tag at best.
research.oio.chartAlt: Bars counting named exceptions by cluster: PKM and markdown tools 5, hosted and open-source memory products 3, formal foundations 5.
research.acs.heading: The field cannot agree on a collision
research.acs.body: ACS gives the agents one shared, versioned surface to work from. Four incompatible ways of handling a contradiction exist at the same time.
research.acs.chartTitle: Correct updates reach 37% at a million-token history, omissions reach 98%
research.acs.chartSubtitle: Upper end of each range reported by HaluMem at 1M-token histories
research.acs.chartCaption: The bars mark the top of each reported range. The ranges are wide because the benchmark measured several systems: correct updates fell to between 1.5% and 37%, omission rose to between 62% and 98%.
research.acs.chartAlt: Two bars at one-million-token histories: correct updates up to 37 percent, omissions up to 98 percent.
research.acs.regimeHeading: Four regimes, none of them compatible
research.acs.regimeNote: No two clusters agree on what to do when a new fact contradicts an old one.
research.acs.statVisibilityLabel: best model, catching a superseded fact it can already see
research.cgm.heading: Adding memory made agreement worse
research.cgm.body: CGM decides what the output says and whether the evidence supports it. This is why a written citation on the item is a requirement.
research.cgm.chartTitle: The same model went from 1.6% sycophancy to 40.2% once Mem0 held the history
research.cgm.chartSubtitle: Sycophancy rate for Sonnet 4.6, chat history versus Mem0 memory
research.cgm.chartCaption: The authors name memory extraction as the primary culprit and call the effect a systemic property of the memory layer. It appeared across Mem0, MemOS and Zep in five model families, up to 40% over in-context baselines.
research.cgm.chartAlt: Two bars for one model: 1.6 percent sycophancy with chat history, 40.2 percent with Mem0 memory.
research.train.heading: The relationship is recorded and never used
research.train.body: train pins versions once, so no repository certifies its own siblings. A superseded fact ages the same way: someone writes down the relationship, then nothing acts on it.
research.train.tableHeading: Four requirements, and what no shipped system provides
research.train.tableNote: Eleven requirements, checked against the closest thing already shipped. These four are the sharpest. Propagation has essentially no precedent.

prd.title: How it works
prd.lede: Five small repositories that give coding agents a shared memory, a shared ticket log, and shared version control. Two minutes, then the map.
prd.what.heading: Five repositories, one layer each
prd.what.body: ACS gives any coding agent on any device the same picture of a project: what is being worked on, who filed it, what was tried, and what happens next. **Agents handle the coordination. A person keeps every decision.**
prd.today.heading: The session ends and the context goes with it
prd.today.body: An agent works inside one conversation. Your project works across months of them. When a conversation closes, the next session starts from whatever you can retype, and the retelling drifts a little each time.
prd.layers.heading: Each layer stores something different
prd.layers.body: One owner per layer, and each of the five says so about itself. Read the third column as the promise: this is the state a fresh agent finds waiting in the repository.
prd.research.heading: Three numbers worth remembering
prd.research.body: Agent memory fails on the way in, and a superseded fact stays believable once it is stored. No benchmark of ACS against either exists yet.
prd.soWhat.write: Most of the damage is done before retrieval can help.
prd.soWhat.staleness: A superseded fact stays on screen, and the agent still acts on it.
prd.soWhat.pin: One number copied thirteen times will drift apart.
prd.next.heading: Open the map and pick your week
prd.next.body: Seventeen points, grouped by the layer that answers each one. Select the failure you have personally paid for and read the line behind it.
prd.details.heading: Check the rest yourself
prd.details.body: What pins what, all seventeen failures, the mechanism, who decides, what is parked, and what nobody has measured.
prd.howto.heading: Open any line yourself
prd.howto.body: Each citation names a repository, a path, a line number and a full commit revision. Open the repository at that revision and read the line. hivemind/research is not a git checkout, so those entries link to the arXiv paper instead.
prd.revisions.heading: Pinned revisions
prd.revisions.note: One full commit revision per repository, current as of 2026-10-13.
prd.edges.heading: What pins what, and what stays separate
prd.edges.body: Every edge comes from a sentence in one of the repositories. ACS runs tickets and does not file them. ACS pins PCM and CGM as external authorities and vendors neither. OIO pins train and preserves its proposed status, and routes README, issue, pull-request and commit prose through CGM. PCM reads versions from the train instead of hand-copying them. OIO took the governance out of the installer and gave it its own repository.
prd.problems.heading: These are the failures, all seventeen
prd.problems.body: Each one states the failure, what it costs a person, and the sentence behind it, with the revision attached.
prd.mechanism.heading: Where the mechanism actually bites
prd.mechanism.body: Three places. The filer stamp is machine-checkable, so an agent cannot promote its own note to a human claim through the body text. Continuity is repository state, so a fresh session reads purpose, current state, bounded task, evidence, blockers and the next action without a prior conversation. Stale projections yield to their field's authority, so a superseded value loses to the field that owns it.
prd.decisions.heading: Every decision stays with a person
prd.decisions.body: Agents break work down, claim tickets and move state forward. Humans own the decisions: what gets prioritised, whose claim counts as human, and which side of a disagreement wins. The stack writes hypotheses and proposed actions, so the record shows what was suggested and who accepted it.
prd.parked.heading: The part that is not finished
prd.parked.body: Adjudication and tie-breaking between agents was JEV's job. JEV is not strong enough for it and is parked in jev-dump. Until it returns, a disagreement between two agents is settled by a person. The stack treats that as the correct outcome.
prd.limits.heading: Nothing here measures ACS
prd.limits.body: Every figure is another group's benchmark of agent memory. They say what the field fails at. No product benchmark of this stack exists yet, and no adoption figure or customer name appears anywhere.
